memory_candidates.content: When a status/policy accuracy fix grows a context/standards/*.md file that is tracked in index-entries.json, check for a companion line_count drift: check-extension-docs.sh's Rule R fails on ANY declared-vs-actual line count mismatch for the edited file, even when the prose content itself is fully correct. Run wc -l on the edited file and update its index-entries.json line_count entry (or run generate-context-line-counts.sh --write) as part of the same edit, not as an afterthought.

Before treating a lint/verification script's non-zero exit as evidence of a regression, compare against baseline via git stash + rerun. A script like check-extension-docs.sh can carry pre-existing, out-of-scope failures (deploy drift, unrelated line_count mismatches) that are indistinguishable from self-caused ones without an explicit baseline diff. This distinguishes 'this task broke something' from 'this was already broken' and prevents scope creep into fixing unrelated infrastructure debt.
